# GEO 入门：如何打造让 ChatGPT 主动推荐的品牌

- 作者：VengeonsP
- 原帖：https://x.com/VengeonsP/status/2115435181037248860
- 发布时间：2026-10-28 21:27（北京时间）
- 收藏日期：2026-10-29
- 内容：中文全文、英文原文；配图保留原图，图中文字未另行翻译。作者的观点与数据按原文保留。

## 中文全文

我会带你看我使用的那份文件：如何让 AI 答案提到我的网站，从品牌提及审计、比较页面，到一份真正能够约束自己的 30 天记分表……

收藏这篇，第 4 部分是你会直接照着用的内容。

要点：

1. AI 答案如何决定提到谁。
2. 你的 AI 据以工作的 GEO 文件。
3. 品牌提及审计。
4. 比较页面和别人的榜单。
5. 30 天记分表。

想为你的业务取得类似结果：[免费试用 ChatSEO 7 天](https://chatseo.app/?utm_source=x&utm_medium=x-article&utm_campaign=geo-101&utm_content=paul&utm_term=en)。

因为 AI 让答案免费了，而一个免费答案只会提到少数几个品牌。

问 ChatGPT“做 X 最好的工具是什么”，你会得到五个名字。问 Google，它的 AI Overview 会给你三四个。问 Perplexity、Gemini 或 Claude，你得到的依然是一份简短名单。

如果你不在这份名单上，对那个买家来说，你就不存在。AI 答案没有第二页。

大多数“GEO 专家”不会告诉你的是：AI 并不是凭空挑选这些名字。它会搜索，阅读有排名的内容，然后重复别人对你的描述。

所以，这篇指南的规则很简单：不要围着 AI 做优化，而要建立 AI 能读到的证据。

这套系统的分工是：

- GEO 文件负责记录：能带来客户的提示词、你的事实资料、证据，以及应该提到你的地方。
- Claude，或者任何能访问搜索数据的智能体，负责枯燥工作：运行提示词、阅读来源、寻找缺口、起草页面。
- 你负责决策、发送邮件和发布。

我们先用今天早上的真实结果页，看看 AI 答案如何挑选名字。然后建立一份文件，审计你在哪里缺席，用页面和外部提及补足，最后用 30 天记分表评估整个过程。

计划如下：

- AI 答案如何决定提到谁。
- GEO 文件：智能体据以工作的一页资料。
- 提及审计：你在哪里缺席，谁取代你被提到。
- 比较页面，以及如何进入他人的榜单。
- 一份真正能够约束自己的 30 天记分表。
- 我这周会做什么。
- Google 的 AI 用我自己的视频来批评我的产品的那一天。
- 这些不能证明什么。
- 第一天就值得照搬的规则。

每一步都包含一项行动、一段可复制的提示词，以及由智能体负责的部分。

我做 SEO 很多年了：先在巴黎一家代理公司工作一年半，之后做自由职业，现在负责 ChatSEO 的 SEO。ChatGPT 曾把我列为法国最好的 SEO 顾问之一，也曾连续几个月不再提到我。我会明确告诉你原因。这两段经历，比任何 GEO 课程教给我的都多。

就是这样。剩下的是具体的基础工作。

## 第 1 部分：AI 答案如何决定提到谁

### 01. 没有 SEO，就没有 GEO

当你问 ChatGPT 一个长问题时，它并不是“知道”答案。遇到近期信息或商业问题，它会运行搜索。

它把你的提示词转化为几个简短的 Google 式查询。“2026 年查看竞争对手流量最好的免费工具是什么”，会变成类似“best free similarweb alternative”“similarweb alternatives 2026”“free website traffic checker”的搜索。然后，它阅读这些查询下有排名的页面，并据此写出答案。

Google 自己也这样说。在它于 2026 年 5 月发布的首份 AI 功能指南中，Google 解释说，AI Overviews 和 AI Mode 运行在传统索引之上，通过所谓的 query fan-out（查询扇出）：一个问题、多次搜索，底层还是常规排名。

所以，GEO 结果跟随 SEO 结果，每次都是如此。如果 AI 执行的搜索中，没有任何与你有关的内容获得排名，它就没有关于你的东西可读。

这也是为什么有人把 GEO 推销成取代 SEO 的新学科时，我会感到不安。它建立在 SEO 之上。先取得排名。实际项目里，大约十项行动中只有一项属于 GEO，另外九项都是传统 SEO。

→ 如果跳过 SEO，GEO 就没有立足点。

### 02. 但排名第一还不够

这是我第一次测量时感到意外的地方。

下面是今天早上截取的美国搜索结果页，查询为“best free similarweb alternative”，处于登录状态，但关闭了个性化。

我们的免费 SimilarWeb 替代工具页面，是第一个自然网页结果。美国 Google 第一名，而且是一个买家搜索词。

可就在它上面的 AI Overview，引用了另外三个网站：similarwebalternative.com、IPRoyal 和 elevatedsignal。点击“Show all”，还会看到两个 YouTube 视频。没有我们。

再读一遍：AI 看得到我们的页面，页面排名第一，但 AI 仍然用别人的榜单来构建答案。

为什么？因为 AI 要回答的是“最好的替代方案有哪些”。第三方写的清单看起来是在回答这个问题；清单中某款工具自己写的页面，即使诚实，看起来也像销售页。

→ 你的网站让你进入搜索，别人的页面让你进入答案。

### 03. AI 引用的是段落，不是整页

看看 AI Overview 展示的三个来源中，有两个的摘要分别以“Table_title: Which SimilarWeb Alternative Should You Use?”和“Table_title: What are the best Similarweb alternatives?”开头。它摘取的是比较表格。

AI 不像人一样读网页。它抓取能直接回答问题的段落：

- 开头几行的直接答案。
- 带编号的排名，每一项用一句话解释“为什么”。
- 能核查事实的表格：价格、免费方案、最适合谁。

一篇 3,000 词的长文，如果始终没有说“对 X 来说最佳选择是 Y，因为 Z”，就没有给 AI 可引用的内容。一张清晰的表格，则给了它现成答案。

→ 写出你希望 AI 重复的那句话，并把它放在容易摘取的位置。

### 04. 真正重要的是评估型搜索

不是所有查询都值得在 GEO 上争取。“什么是 GEO”会被 AI 从上百个可互换的页面中直接回答，谁都得不到功劳。

钱在评估型搜索里，也就是人们即将做选择时输入的那些查询：

- “best（你的品类）（年份）”。
- “（竞争对手）alternative”和“（竞争对手）alternatives free”。
- “（工具 A）vs（工具 B）”。
- “（你的品牌）review”“（你的品牌）pricing”。
- “best（服务）in（城市）”。

这些提示词会让 AI 给出名字。对于这些搜索，标题中的年份像一个作弊码：ChatGPT 经常自行给搜索加上当前年份，因此带“2026”的标题，恰好匹配它输入的内容。

→ 选那些会让 AI 报出名字的提示词，其余先忽略。

### 05. AI 从哪里读取关于你的信息

根据我从 2025 年以来在自己的网站和 ChatSEO 上看到的情况，AI 答案会从下面这些地方找到推荐的名字，我会按这个顺序开展工作：

- 别人写的榜单：有排名网站上的“最佳 X”文章、比较表和盘点。
- 社区：有排名的 Reddit 帖子、论坛、Quora 和 LinkedIn 帖子。
- YouTube：在同一搜索中有排名的视频及其文字稿。
- 评价平台：软件行业的 Trustpilot 和 G2，本地商家的 Google Business Profile。
- 你自己的页面：比较页、“替代方案”页、定价页和关于页。

对于“最佳 X”提示词，你的网站排在这份清单的最后。对于“（你的品牌）review”和“（你的品牌）pricing”，它排第一，因为这时候你就是讨论对象。

→ 大多数 AI 推荐来自第三方页面。按这个事实分配精力。

## 第 2 部分：你的 AI 据以工作的 GEO 文件

### 06. 为什么是一份文件，而不是一次聊天

大多数人所谓的“做 GEO”，就是问一次 ChatGPT 是否知道自己的品牌，然后慌了，再写三篇博客。

一个月后再问，得到不同答案，却根本不知道自己做的事情有没有效果。

解决办法很无聊，但有效：建立一份文件，写好后每周更新，记录开展工作所依赖的一切。智能体每次工作前都读它，你每次决策前也读它。

我把它保存为名叫 GEO.md 的纯文本文件，放在运行 Claude Code 的文件夹里。你也可以放在 Google Docs。格式不重要，写下来才重要。

第一天，我会粘贴下面这个框架：

```markdown
# GEO.md（一份文件，每周一更新）

## 1. 我们是谁：用一段可核查的文字说明
（卖什么、卖给谁、价格范围、所在国家、创立年份、创始人姓名。
每一个事实在整个互联网上都必须一致。）

## 2. 能带来客户的提示词（10—20 个）
（买家在做选择前会输入的问题。每行一个，
同时列出 AI 为回答它而执行的 Google 式查询。）

## 3. 今天谁被提到了
（每个提示词：AI 提到的品牌、引用的来源、日期。）

## 4. 证据库
（仅限我们能提供截图的数字，每个数字附来源和日期。）

## 5. 来源地图
（AI 为回答我们的提示词而阅读的榜单、帖子、视频、评价页面，
以及其中有没有我们。）

## 6. 我们自己的评估页面
（比较、替代方案、定价、评价页面：URL、目标查询、
Google 排名、上次检查时间。）

## 7. 拒绝事项清单
（绝不做什么：绝不在自己的榜单上把自己排第一；
绝不买假评价；绝不发布无法提供截图的数字。）

## 8. 记分表
（30 天内的数据，逐周记录。）
```

就这些，八个模块。本指南的一切最终都会进入这份文件。

### 07. 模块 1：一段话，各处一致

AI 答案是对互联网共识的总结。如果你的首页说创立于 2023 年，LinkedIn 写 2024 年，某个目录又说你位于另一个国家，AI 就会得到三个版本的你，而且没有哪个版本能让它确信。

所以第一项工作，是把关于你的事实写成一段陌生人能够核查的文字，再让每个资料页说同样的话：关于页、LinkedIn 公司页、Google Business Profile（如果有）、Product Hunt 或 Crunchbase 页面，以及作者简介框。

一些小技术项也放在这里，我想坦诚说明它们的分量。带有社交资料 sameAs 字段的 Organization 结构化数据、含真实姓名和简介的作者框、法律声明页面，智能体大约 20 分钟就能加齐。做一次即可。这是基础卫生，不是主要增长手段。

→ 缺乏清楚身份的网站，在 Google 上很脆弱，在 AI 答案里难以被看见。

### 08. 模块 2：能带来客户的提示词

这是最重要的模块。人们往往写下自己希望买家输入的提示词，因此把它做错。

别猜。从买家已经在输入的内容开始：

- 销售电话和私信中人们问你的问题。
- Search Console 中包含 best、vs、alternative、review、pricing 的查询。
- 主要买家搜索里的“People also ask”问题框。
- Bing Webmaster Tools 中的 grounding queries（依据查询，第 3 部分会进一步介绍）。

然后，把每个问题写成一个人会怎样问 AI，而不是怎样输入 Google。“小型代理公司最适合的 SimilarWeb 免费替代方案是什么？”是提示词；“similarweb alternative free”是 AI 为此执行的搜索。你需要把二者并列记录。

把下面这段粘贴到 Claude，或者 ChatGPT，这一步用哪一个都无所谓：

```text
你正在帮我列出能带来客户的 AI 提示词。

我的业务：（模块 1 的一段介绍）
买家的真实问题（销售电话、私信、回复）：（粘贴）
Search Console 中含 best / vs / alternative / review / pricing 的查询：
（粘贴导出数据：查询 + 展示次数）

1. 写出 15 个真实买家在选择像我这样的服务商之前，会输入 ChatGPT 的提示词。
   使用自然语言，每行一个。
2. 每个提示词列出 AI 为回答它而执行的 2—4 个简短 Google 式查询（查询扇出）。
3. 给每个提示词标记 EVALUATION（最终给出名字）或 INFO（最终给出解释）。
   删除 INFO 类。
4. 按提问者距离付款的远近，对剩余项排序。
不要把我没有提供的查询编造成“真实查询”。你自己提出的建议标为 SUGGESTED。
```

保留 10—20 个。再多就很难认真追踪。

→ 真正检查的十个提示词，胜过从来不检查的一百个。

### 09. 模块 4：证据库

人人都跳过证据库，但恰恰是它，让 AI 不只报出你的名字，还说出你的优点。

当 AI 推荐一个工具，它会附带理由：“最适合小网站”“最便宜”“代理公司在用”。这个理由来自它找到的文字。如果关于你的文字只有自己的营销内容，推荐理由就会很含糊。

因此，把你有权引用的真实结果列出来，每项都有截图和日期：

- 客户成果：“6 个月内，Google 每日点击量从约 40 增加到超过 200，收入增长至 3 倍。”这是我们一位电商客户本月分享的结果。
- 你能展示的使用数据。
- 奖项，或者别人发布的关于你的排名。
- 带有方法说明的公开测试。

然后，在各处以相同方式使用它们：自己的页面、客座文章、Reddit 回复和 YouTube 描述。跨来源重复出现，会被 AI 读成共识。

保护你的规则是：没有来源，就不能进入证据库。任何人，包括你自己，都不能以你的名义编造数字。一项被引用回来的假数据，损失比十项真数据带来的收益更大。

→ 只有其他页面先重复你的推荐理由，AI 才会重复它。

### 10. 模块 7：拒绝事项清单

写下你不会做什么。听起来像小事，但它能防止 GEO 项目在第二个月变成垃圾推广：容易的机会用尽后，总会有人建议走捷径。

我的清单是：

- 绝不在自己的“最佳”榜单中把自己排第一。
- 绝不发布拿不出截图的数字。
- 绝不买评价，也绝不以任何东西交换评价。
- 绝不在两个 Reddit 帖子里发布相同的推广评论。
- 绝不加一份 llms.txt 就说自己做了 GEO。
- 绝不在希望被引用的页面上屏蔽 AI 爬虫。
- 预算不多时，绝不为“GEO 可见度分数”付费。

每一条都来自我尝试过或亲眼看过失败的事情。第一条让我付出的代价最大，我会在第 4 部分再谈。

### 用 Claude 建立文件

八个模块不用手工填写。对于能搜索互联网的智能体，我会用以下提示词生成初稿：

```text
阅读我的网站（首页、关于页、定价页、博客目录）：（URL）
阅读我的 LinkedIn 公司页，以及 Google Business Profile（如有）。

按照下面的 8 个模块建立 GEO.md。规则：
- 模块 1：一段事实介绍。列出所有来源间存在差异的事实
  （创立年份、地点、价格、创始人）。
- 模块 2：留空，由我根据自己的数据填写。
- 模块 4：仅使用你在页面上找到的数字，附 URL，绝不估算。
- 模块 6：列出网站上所有比较、替代方案、定价和评价页面，
  以及它们看起来针对的搜索。
- 模块 3、5、8：留空，内容来自审计。
- 模块 7：原样复制我的拒绝事项清单：（粘贴）
最后，列出互联网上关于我们最不一致的 5 项事实，并指出每个版本在哪里。
```

最后那份不一致清单，才是真正有价值的东西。先修正它。

## 第 3 部分：品牌提及审计

### 11. 在私密环境中手动运行提示词

现在，查清自己处于什么位置。我要说一句不受欢迎的话：手动做。

每周一，在无痕浏览、退出登录或临时聊天中，在 ChatGPT、Google（AI Overview 和 AI Mode），以及买家使用的另一款助手中，运行 3—5 个提示词。只要 15 分钟。

为什么手动？因为付费 GEO 追踪工具会测试根本没人输入的提示词，生成数千个变体，再卖给你一个建立在它们之上的“可见度分数”。预算少的时候，付费工具是最差的选择：贵，而且存在偏差。等到确实需要每周大规模使用，再用 Claude 建一个小型内部工具。在那之前，你自己的眼睛就是最好的追踪器。

每个提示词，在文件的模块 3 里写三件事：

- 答案给出的名字，按顺序记录。
- 它引用的来源：链接、AI Overviews 的“Show all”。
- 日期。

我把结果粘贴进下面这个模板：

```text
提示词：小型代理公司最好的 SimilarWeb 免费替代方案是什么？
日期：2026-10-28   平台：Google AI Overview（美国，私密会话）
提到的名字：Semrush、Similarweb 扩展、SparkToro、Ahrefs 免费工具、GA、GSC
引用：similarwebalternative.com、iproyal.com、elevatedsignal.com、
      YouTube（GEO Mastery with Adam）、YouTube（AllAboutAI）
提到我们：否   引用我们：否   我们的 Google 排名：第 1
（查询：best free similarweb alternative）
下一步：进入 3 个被引用榜单中的 1 个，做 1 条视频
```

“下一步”那行才是重点。没有下一步行动的审计，只是附带电子表格的焦虑。

→ 被引用的来源，就是你的待办清单。

### 12. 阅读你已经拥有的免费 GEO 数据

有一个真实且免费的 GEO 数据来源：Bing Webmaster Tools 的 AI Performance 报告。它展示你的页面在微软 AI 答案中被引用了多少次、哪些页面被引用，以及 grounding queries——AI 在引用你之前实际输入的搜索。

最后这一项对模块 2 极有价值。这些不是某个工具编出来的提示词，而是 AI 真正执行过的搜索。

举个今年早些时候的规模例子：在我的法语咨询网站上，“agence GEO”页面在三个月内被引用 928 次；表现最好的“meilleur freelance GEO”页面，30 天内接近 400 次，当月全站约 830 次引用。

如果还没连接 Bing Webmaster Tools，今天就连接。从 Search Console 导入，只要五分钟。

### 13. 建立来源地图：谁提到了你，谁没有

## Google 的 AI 用我自己的视频来批评我的产品的那一天

讲个小故事，因为它改变了我对这一切的看法。

9 月，我查看 Google AI Overview 如何评价 ChatSEO。它列出产品的一些缺点。这很合理，每个产品都有不足。

随后，我看这些观点来自哪里。它们来自我自己，来自我自己的一条 YouTube 视频。

有两条教训。我认为它们几乎把整个 GEO 浓缩在一屏里。

第一：AI 会读所有关于你的内容，包括你自己说的话，而且会像引用评价一样，自信地引用这些内容。YouTube 对 Google 答案的供给作用，远比人们想象的大。

第二：你躲不开，也不该尝试躲。你能做的是让事实保持最新。当某个不足修复后，在同样的地方明确说出来，并写上日期。AI 会重复那个最新、也被重复最多的你。

## 这些不能证明什么

我想坦诚交代局限，因为 GEO 领域充满了承诺。

- **不能保证你会被提到。** AI 答案因人、日期、国家和问法而异。这里的一切只是在提高概率。没有人能保证提及，能这么保证的人是在卖分数。
- **被提到不一定是你的工作造成的。** 本月我重新启动了一个联盟营销网站作为副业，没有做任何 GEO，就收到一条来自 ChatGPT 的线索。有时候 AI 就是会找到你。别把功劳算给没有发生过的行动。
- **一个结果页只是一个结果页。** 第 1 部分的截图只是某个早晨、一个国家、一次搜索。请运行你自己的搜索。
- **没有 SEO，提及不会持久。** 如果页面没有排名，也没人链接你，支撑你的就只剩那些提到你的榜单，而榜单会被重写。
- **流量数据并不完整。** 复制粘贴品牌名、不传递来源信息的助手、问过 AI 后直接打电话的人，很多 AI 影响永远不会显示为“AI 流量”。
- **llms.txt、痴迷 schema 和“内容分块”都不是主要增长手段。** Google 自己的指南说，AI 功能运行在传统索引之上。把结构化数据做一次，然后回到真正能推动结果的工作。

## 第一天就值得照搬的规则

## Part 1: How AI answers decide who to name

01. There is no GEO without SEO

When you ask ChatGPT a long question, it doesn't "know" the answer. On anything recent or commercial, it runs searches

It takes your prompt and turns it into a few short, Google-style queries. "What's the best free tool to check a competitor's traffic in 2026" becomes something like "best free similarweb alternative", "similarweb alternatives 2026", "free website traffic checker". Then it reads the pages that rank for those queries and writes its answer from them

Google said it itself. In its first guide on AI features, published in May 2026, it explained that AI Overviews and AI Mode run on the classic index, through what it calls query fan-out: one question, many searches, the usual ranking underneath

So GEO results follow SEO results. Every time. If nothing about you ranks for the searches the AI runs, the AI has nothing to read about you

This is why I get nervous when someone sells "GEO" as a new discipline that replaces SEO. It sits on top of SEO. Rank first. In a real campaign, roughly one action in ten is GEO. The other nine are classic SEO

-> If you skip the SEO, the GEO has nothing to stand on

02. But ranking first is not enough

Here is the part that surprised me the first time I measured it

This is the US results page for "best free similarweb alternative", captured this morning, logged in, personalization off:

![原图](<../../90_附件/配图/2115435181037248860-2.jpg>)

Our free SimilarWeb alternative page is the first web result. Number one on Google, in the US, on a buyer search

And the AI Overview right above it quotes three other sites: [similarwebalternative.com](//similarwebalternative.com), IPRoyal and elevatedsignal. Click "Show all" and you find two YouTube videos as well. Not us

Read that again: the AI sees our page, it ranks first, and the AI still builds its answer from other people's lists

Why? Because of what the AI is trying to do. It is answering "what are the best alternatives". A list written by a third party looks like an answer to that question. A page written by one of the tools in the list looks like a sales page, even when it's honest

-> Your own site gets you into the search. Other people's pages get you into the answer

03. AIs quote passages, not pages

Look at the snippets the AI Overview shows for two of those three sources: they start with "Table_title: Which SimilarWeb Alternative Should You Use?" and "Table_title: What are the best Similarweb alternatives?". What it lifted is their comparison tables

The AI doesn't read a page like a human. It grabs the passages that answer the question directly:

- a direct answer in the first lines
- a numbered ranking with one line of "why" per item
- a table of facts that can be checked: price, free plan, best for

A 3,000-word essay that never says "the best option for X is Y, because Z" gives the AI nothing to quote. A page with a clean table gives it a ready-made answer

-> Write the sentence you want the AI to repeat, and put it where it can be lifted

04. The searches that matter are evaluation searches

Not every query is worth fighting for in GEO. "What is GEO" will be answered by the AI itself, from a hundred interchangeable pages. Nobody gets the credit

The money is in evaluation searches, the ones someone types when they are about to choose:

- "best (your category) (year)"
- "(competitor) alternative" and "(competitor) alternatives free"
- "(tool A) vs (tool B)"
- "(your brand) review", "(your brand) pricing"
- "best (service) in (city)"

These are the prompts where the AI gives names. And they are the searches where the year in the title acts like a cheat code: ChatGPT adds the current year to a lot of its searches on its own, so a title with "2026" in it matches what it types

-> Pick the prompts where an AI hands out names, and ignore the rest

- lists written by others: "best X" articles on sites that rank, comparison tables, roundups
- communities: Reddit threads, forums, Quora, LinkedIn posts that rank
- YouTube: videos that rank on the same search, and their transcripts
- review platforms: Trustpilot and G2 for software, the Google Business Profile for a local business
- your own pages: comparison pages, "alternative to" pages, pricing, the about page

Your own site is last on that list for the "best X" prompts. It comes first for "(your brand) review" and "(your brand) pricing", because there, you ARE the subject

-> Most AI recommendations come from third-party pages. Plan your effort that way

Most people "do GEO" by asking ChatGPT once whether it knows their brand, panicking, and writing three blog posts

Then a month later they ask again, get a different answer, and have no idea whether anything they did worked

The fix is boring and it works: one file, written once, updated every week, that holds everything the work depends on. Your agent reads it before every job. You read it before every decision

I keep it as a plain text file called GEO.md in the folder where I run Claude Code. You can keep it in a Google Doc. The format doesn't matter. Writing it down does

Here's the skeleton I'd paste on day one:

```

(what we sell, to whom, the price range, the country, the founding year,
the founders' names. Every fact must be the same everywhere on the web)

## 2. The prompts that pay (10 to 20)

(the 30-day numbers, week by week)
```

That's it. Eight blocks. Everything in this guide ends up in that file

07. Block 1: one paragraph, the same everywhere

An AI answer is a summary of what the web agrees on. If your homepage says you were founded in 2023, LinkedIn says 2024, and a directory says you're based in another country, the AI has three versions of you, and none of them is confident

So the first job is to write the facts about you once, in one paragraph a stranger could check, and then make every profile say the same thing: your about page, your LinkedIn company page, your Google Business Profile if you have one, your Product Hunt or Crunchbase page, your author boxes

This is also where the small technical bits go, and I want to be honest about their weight. Organization structured data with your social profiles in "sameAs", an author box with a real name and a bio, legal pages: an agent adds all of it in about 20 minutes. Do it once. It's hygiene, not the lever

-> A site with no clear identity is fragile in Google and invisible in AI answers

08. Block 2: the prompts that pay

This is the most important block, and the one people get wrong by writing the prompts they WISH buyers typed

Don't guess. Start from what your buyers already type:

- the questions people ask you on sales calls and in DMs
- your Search Console queries that contain "best", "vs", "alternative", "review", "pricing"
- the "People also ask" boxes on your main buyer searches
- the "grounding queries" in Bing Webmaster Tools (more on that in Part 3)

Then write each one the way a person would ask an AI, not the way they'd type into Google. "What's the best free alternative to SimilarWeb for a small agency?" is a prompt. "similarweb alternative free" is the search the AI will run for it. You want both, side by side

-> Ten prompts you actually check beat a hundred you don't

09. Block 4: the proof bank

The proof bank is the block everyone skips, and it is the one that makes AI answers say good things about you instead of just your name

When an AI recommends a tool, it attaches a reason: "best for small sites", "cheapest", "used by agencies". That reason comes from text it found. If the only text about you is your own marketing, the reason will be vague

So list the real results you are allowed to cite, each one with a screenshot and a date:

- a customer result: "from about 40 to more than 200 Google clicks a day in 6 months, revenue x3" (one of our customers, an e-commerce shop, shared this month)
- a usage number you can show
- an award, a ranking someone else published about you
- a public test with its method

Then use them, the same way, everywhere: on your pages, in your guest posts, in your replies on Reddit, in your YouTube descriptions. Repetition across sources is what an AI reads as consensus

And the rule that protects you: nothing goes in the proof bank without a source. Nobody, you included, ever invents a number under your name. One fake figure that gets quoted back at you costs more than ten real ones earn

-> The AI repeats your reason only if other pages repeat it first

Write down what you will not do. It sounds like a detail. It is what keeps a GEO campaign from turning into spam in month two, when the easy wins are gone and someone suggests a shortcut

Mine:

- I never rank myself first in my own "best" list
- I never post a number I can't screenshot
- I never buy reviews, and never ask for a review in exchange for anything
- I never post the same promotional comment in two Reddit threads
- I never add an llms.txt file and call it GEO
- I never block AI crawlers on pages I want quoted
- I never pay for a "GEO visibility score" on a small budget

- screenshots of the real tools, never a mock-up
- the date it was last checked

Here's the prompt I use to brief one:

```
Search: (competitor) alternative
Read the 10 results on page one for this search (only page one).

1. What type of page did Google choose? (list, comparison, tool, article)
2. Which tools do the top 3 name, and in what order?
3. Which facts do they all give (price, free plan, best for)? Which facts
   does none of them give?
4. Draft my page:
   - title: the search first, a colon, a count, the current year
   - first 3 lines: the direct answer
   - a comparison table with checkable facts only, each with its source
   - a one-line verdict per tool, first person
   - my brand as a numbered entry, never number 1, with a disclosure line
   - one thing the top 3 don't have: a test, a number, a screenshot
Flag every fact you could not verify on the tool's own site.
```

-> Own every search where your brand is the subject

16. Never rank yourself first. I learned it the expensive way

In 2025, I taught the opposite. My advice was: write a "best SEO consultants in France" page, put yourself first, and ChatGPT will repeat it

And it worked. From June to August 2025, ChatGPT named me first for "best SEO consultant in France", quoting my own page

Then it stopped working. In January 2026 I was third. By July 2026, ChatGPT wasn't citing my own site at all anymore for that prompt. The AIs had caught on: a list written by one of its entries is a sales page, and they started citing the second and third names of such lists rather than the author

The numbers we built ChatSEO's GEO playbook on say the same thing: since January 2026, sites that ranked themselves first across many "best" pages lost 29 to 49% of their Google visibility, and when an AI Overview cited one of those self-ranked lists, it recommended a rival 69% of the time

So I had Claude remove my on-site self-rankings. On the ChatSEO blog, ChatSEO stays a numbered entry in its own lists, somewhere between second and seventh, with a disclosure. Never first

Look back at the competitor's list in Part 3. They put themselves first. If the research above holds, that number one helps the second name more than it helps them

-> Rank by truth, say where you fit, concede where a rival wins

17. Get into other people's lists

If the AI quotes third-party lists, the job is to be in them

What brought me back into ChatGPT's answers was not a better page on my site. It was other people's pages. I did ranking exchanges: a place in my list for a place in theirs, with people in a neighboring field, not competitors

The cleanest one was with an agency called Convertix. My list of the best Meta Ads agencies in 2026, which is their field, not mine, came out of an exchange with them. We exchanged two rankings in total, and ChatGPT named me among the best SEO consultants in France again, this time through their pages and my exchanges, not through my own site

Exchanges beat paying. A paid placement on a site that sells placements to everyone is a list nobody trusts, AI included. A list written by a real business, on a site that ranks, about its own field, is the real thing

How to find the lists worth being in:

- your source map, status OUT-REACHABLE, sorted by how many prompts cite them
- the top 10 for "best (your category) (year)" in every country you sell in
- lists on sites in a NEIGHBORING field, which can rank you without ranking a competitor of theirs

The outreach email is short, and it offers something first:

```
Subject: your list of (category) for 2026

Hi (first name),

I read your list of the best (category) for 2026. (One specific, true
line about it.)

I run (brand), (one line from GEO.md block 1). I'm putting together a
list of the best (their category) and I'd like to include (their brand),
with an honest one-line verdict.

If you think we'd fit in your list too, here are the facts you'd need:
(3 checkable facts + one screenshot link). No problem if not.

(Your name)
```

Asking for the top spot in THEIR list is fair: it's their list, and in my view that's most of what GEO adds to SEO, other sites that rank you first on the "best" searches. Never pay. And only offer a place in your list if they would genuinely deserve it there, or the whole thing turns into a link scheme

-> One list that ranks and gets quoted beats ten you paid for

18. Reviews, threads and videos

E-reputation is, as I keep saying, the SEO and GEO cheat code of the year. Three more kinds of sources to work on:

Review platforms. For software, Trustpilot and G2. For a local business, the Google Business Profile. An AI asked "is (brand) good?" reads those first. Ask for reviews at the right moment: right after you solved someone's support problem is when people say yes. Answer every review, the negative ones first

Reddit and forums. The threads in your source map are open. Answer the question that was asked, fully, as a person, and mention your product only where it genuinely answers it, with "I built this" in plain words. And be careful: our Reddit channel once brought 2,000 waiting-list signups to ChatSEO, then our main account got banned and we lost it. One account, real answers, no copy-pasted promo, ever

YouTube. Two of the five sources in that AI Overview were YouTube videos. Video is hard to fake, so AIs and Google trust it. I've seen my own video and its Short both show up in Google's AI Overview for a "(tool) review" search, while ranking first on YouTube. A "review" or "vs" video with the search in its title is one of the least contested places left

-> Be present where the AI reads, under your own name

19. Fix the sources that get you wrong

The cheapest GEO win is rarely a new mention. It's an old one that's wrong

Go back to your source map and filter on IN-WRONG. In my experience, this list is longer than people expect: an old price, a feature you removed, a plan that no longer exists, a description of what you did two years ago, a founder who left

Every one of those is a sentence an AI can repeat about you tomorrow, with full confidence. And unlike a new list, a correction costs the other site almost nothing: they don't have to add anyone, they just have to update a line

Three rules for asking:

- One email, one fix. Quote their exact sentence, give the right fact, link the page on your site that proves it
- Make it easy. Write the corrected sentence for them, in their style, ready to paste
- Give them a reason that helps them. An outdated price makes their page look abandoned, to readers and to Google. You're helping them keep it fresh

Here's the prompt to draft them in one go:

```
Below are the sources from my audit with status IN-WRONG. For each one:
- the URL
- the exact sentence about my brand
- the correct fact (from GEO.md block 1, with the URL that proves it)

Write one short email per source:
- subject: "small correction on your (page topic) page"
- 4 lines max: what's outdated, the corrected sentence ready to paste,
  the proof link, thanks
- no ask for a link, no ask for a better position, no attachment
Then list the sources where no contact email is visible, and where I
could find one (author page, contact form, LinkedIn).
```

Then track them in block 5. When a page gets corrected, change its status to IN-GOOD and write the date. Two weeks later, run the prompts that cited it and see whether the answer changed. That's the cleanest cause and effect you'll ever get in GEO

-> A wrong mention is worse than no mention. Fix it first

## Part 5: The 30-day scorecard

20. Why 30 days, and why a scorecard

GEO has a measuring problem. AI answers change from one day to the next, from one person to the next. If you check once and look at whether your name is there, you'll either celebrate a fluke or panic over one

A scorecard fixes that. Same prompts, same conditions, same day every week, written down. After four weeks you see a trend instead of a mood

And 30 days is the honest horizon for the first verdict on mentions, not on pages. A new or changed page needs about three months in Google before you judge it: Google keeps it in a transition for roughly 90 days, and editing it again during that window restarts the clock. So in 30 days you judge what you DID (lists joined, corrections made, pages published), and the first movements in answers. You judge the pages at 90

## The day Google's AI quoted my own video against my product

A small story, because it changed how I think about all this

In September, I looked at what Google's AI Overview said about ChatSEO. It listed negative points about the product. Fair enough, every product has some

Then I looked at where those points came from. They came from me. From one of my own YouTube videos

Two lessons, and I think they're the whole of GEO in one screen

First: the AI reads everything about you, including what you said yourself, and it quotes it with the same confidence as a review. YouTube feeds Google's answers far more than people think

Second: you can't hide from it, and you shouldn't try. What you can do is keep the facts current. When a weakness gets fixed, say so, in the same places, with the date. The AI repeats the most recent, most repeated version of you

## What this does not prove

I want to be honest about the limits, because the GEO space is full of promises

- It doesn't guarantee you'll be named. AI answers vary by person, by day, by country and by how the question is phrased. Everything here raises the odds. Nobody can promise you a mention, and anyone who does is selling a score
- Being named isn't always caused by your work. I relaunched an affiliate site as a side project this month and got a lead from ChatGPT with zero GEO work on it. Sometimes the AI just finds you. Don't credit an action that didn't happen
- One result page is one result page. The capture in Part 1 is one search, one country, one morning. Run your own
- Mentions without SEO don't last. If your pages don't rank and nobody links to you, the lists that mention you will be the only thing holding you up, and lists get rewritten
- The traffic numbers are incomplete. Copy-pasted brand names, assistants that don't pass a referrer, people who ask the AI and then call you: a lot of AI influence never shows up as "AI traffic"
- llms.txt, schema obsession and "content chunking" aren't the lever. Google's own guide says AI features run on the classic index. Do the structured data once, then go back to the work that moves things

## The rules I'd copy on day one

- Rank first, then GEO. No page that ranks for the searches the AI runs, no mention to read
- Pick evaluation prompts. The ones that end with names: best, vs, alternative, review, pricing
- Write one file. GEO.md, eight blocks, updated every Monday
- Facts identical everywhere. One paragraph, copied to every profile
- Third parties over your own site for "best X" prompts
- Never rank yourself first in your own list. A numbered place lower down, with a disclosure, is fine
- Exchange, don't pay, for a place in a list. Neighboring fields, not competitors
- Track 3 to 5 prompts a week by hand, in private sessions. Read Bing's AI Performance report, it's free
- Three actions a week, maximum. One outreach, one owned page, one community or video
- Judge mentions at 30 days, pages at 90. And never edit a page during its first three months
